## Findings
- claim-1: The two Theorem 5.4 families have \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators, with \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6@L14-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The paper’s reported computation covers only \(r\le4,\ q=n-r\le5\). [source-6@L46-L54|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-3: For \((r,q,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\), \(a=3\), \(b=2\), hence \(N=\binom53=10\). The two specialized families are \[ F_1=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55), \] \[ F_2=(22,221,2211,222,22111,2221,22211,2222,22221,22222). \]
- claim-4: The truncated Pieri presentation has \(431\) Schur-basis columns and \(2130\) Pieri rows. Complementary-column eliminations for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) use only unit pivots and leave no residual relation; the computed quotient is \(\mathbb Z^{10}\), with either family giving a basis. [artifact 0b05e147fd3b8f028a0683ee0de19704b04f214954cc0d8c387547f8371d7299]
- claim-5: Assuming the standard identification \(A_+J_v=\sum_{k=1}^{6}h_kJ_v\) and that these two families generate \(J_v\), the computation implies both families are irredundant generators of \(J_v\), by graded Nakayama.
## Strategy
Treat the \((r,q,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\) result as an artifact-backed finite Pieri-lattice computation. Use the box quotient and \(A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_6)\) to present \(J_v/A_+J_v\), then test each ten-element proposed family as complementary free columns. The critic audit confirms the unit-pivot elimination invariant, conditional on the artifact.

## Gaps
The computation is not independently reproduced: both horizontal-strip enumerators share partition infrastructure, and no direct-LR or independent Smith-form calculation was supplied. The artifact output lacks transformed pivot relations, so it is not a compact standalone unimodular certificate. Irredundance remains conditional on the stated box-model, Pieri-presentation, and generation hypotheses.

## Next
Produce either:
1. an independently written exact LR/Smith computation for this case; or  
2. a compact certificate listing transformed pivot relations, the unimodular complementary minor, and integral reduction of every relation row.

No uniform conclusion beyond this finite case is established.
